speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are concerned about your infant's bilious vomiting, inability to pass meconium, and abdominal distension. To determine the cause, has there been any family history of intestinal obstructions or Down syndrome?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease or meconium ileus. Given the home birth and the classic triad of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium, and abdominal distension, I must rule out midgut volvulus. Please confirm if the stool is currently present or absent, and request an abdominal X-ray immediately. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.
